sources.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, Physical Review D 50 (1994), 846–864, arXiv:gr-qc/9403028v1
sources.locator: Complete 31-page PDF retrieved. Read §3, equations (40)–(48), printed pp. 8–9 (PDF pp. 9–10), and §4, equations (49)–(60), printed pp. 10–11 (PDF pp. 11–12). This includes both potential ambiguities, the Iyer–Wald current ordering, on-shell closure, local exactness, the finite-boundary-flux caveat, and the general Noether-charge decomposition. The asymptotic falloff discussion is read only as a boundary-condition warning.

contents.name: Equations (40)–(43): the two potential ambiguities, theta to theta + delta mu + dY
contents.support: §3, printed pp. 8–9: the exact Lagrangian shift contributes delta mu to the chosen potential, while the independent exact-form shift is dY. The item expands both commuting variations and proves that only the d(delta2 Y(delta1) - delta1 Y(delta2)) term remains.

contents.name: Equations (44)–(47): Iyer–Wald symplectic-current order and its integrated boundary ambiguity
contents.support: §3, printed p. 9: omega is defined as delta2 theta(delta1) - delta1 theta(delta2), and the integrated form receives only the Y corner contribution. The current definition preserves this sign order; the local ambiguity proof derives the compact-chain boundary formula.

contents.name: Equation (50): dJ = -E dot Lie_xi(phi), and equations (49)–(51): local on-shell charge
contents.support: §4, printed pp. 10–11: the current is theta(phi; Lie_xi phi) - i_xi L, its divergence is minus the Euler form paired with the diffeomorphism variation, and a closed on-shell current has a local primitive. The item proves the identity and supplies a local star-shaped homotopy primitive, without asserting a global charge.

contents.name: Equations (52)–(60): general higher-derivative Noether-charge decomposition and its ambiguity
contents.support: The current batch proves the off-shell current identity and local exactness only. It does not construct the higher-derivative decomposition of a globally defined Noether charge.
contents.reason: The assigned claim derives the off-shell current identity and local exactness only; the general higher-derivative decomposition would add a separate construction and ambiguity analysis.

contents.name: Noncompact Cauchy surfaces and asymptotic falloff conditions
contents.support: §3 discusses convergence and cut independence near spatial infinity. The assigned proposition instead uses finite smooth chains and retains the explicit side-flux term; no asymptotic limit or falloff assumption is used.
contents.reason: The assigned scope is compact finite-region calculus with no boundary at infinity, so asymptotic falloff and convergence of noncompact integrals are separate obligations.

sources.title: Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, lecture notes, arXiv:1801.07064v4
sources.locator: Complete 125-page lecture-note PDF retrieved. Read Lecture 1, §§1.3.1–1.3.3, printed pp. 14–22 (PDF pp. 14–22), and §§1.4.1–1.4.2, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 23–24). This includes the field/parameter-space form conventions, the covariant current, the fundamental surface-charge identity, residual potential ambiguities, and the charge-integrability discussion. The author's field-space sign convention is opposite to the Iyer–Wald order adopted here and was translated explicitly.

contents.name: Section 1.3.1: field fibration, the variational bicomplex, theta, omega and integrated form
contents.support: The notes define field-space variations and the spacetime/field-space form types, then derive the symplectic current and its integral. Their contracted omega has the opposite ordering from Iyer–Wald; the authored definition explicitly uses the task's Iyer–Wald ordering.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3: Noether current, local exactness and the fundamental surface-charge identity
contents.support: The notes derive a diffeomorphism current, its on-shell closure, and local exactness for the Noether charge. The assigned proposition independently proves dJ = -E dot Lie_xi(phi) from the chosen first-variation identity and limits exactness to star-shaped coordinate patches.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3: residual potential ambiguity
contents.support: The notes distinguish the exact Lagrangian shift from the independent potential exact-form shift. The assigned proposition calculates the resulting current change and boundary integral.

contents.name: Section 1.4.1: surface-charge variation integrated along a path in field space
contents.support: This page does not construct a particular codimension-two surface-charge form or a path-integrated charge; it only defines the exactness condition for a proposed variation one-form.
contents.reason: The page defines exactness of a proposed charge-variation one-form but does not construct a particular codimension-two surface-charge form or path-integrated charge.

contents.name: Section 1.4.2: integrability condition for a Hamiltonian generator
contents.support: The notes identify charge variation as a field-space one-form and distinguish local closedness from existence of a Hamiltonian. The definition records global exactness as the required condition and keeps local primitives separate.

contents.name: Section 1.3.2: Noether's second theorem and gauge-identity derivations
contents.support: The assigned result follows directly from the first-variation decomposition and covariance. It does not assert the more general differential-identity construction for arbitrary gauge generators.
contents.reason: The assigned covariance identity follows directly from the chosen first-variation decomposition; the general gauge-identity theorem needs additional gauge-generator hypotheses.

contents.name: Equations (2.17)–(2.27): local variational decomposition, boundary potential and integrated presymplectic form
contents.support: §2.2 gives the first-variation form and explains that the potential is ambiguous by a boundary derivative; the parameter-space exterior derivative supplies the integrated closed two-form. The current definition is conditional on a chosen decomposition and asserts no unique potential.

contents.name: Sections 2.3–2.4: covariance, admissible diffeomorphisms and boundary Hamiltonians
contents.support: The notes distinguish covariance of the Lagrangian from a diffeomorphism preserving boundary conditions and derive boundary Hamiltonians only with specified action-boundary data. The assigned proposition states covariance as an explicit premise and does not claim their Hamiltonian formula.

contents.name: Section 3.2: two-derivative scalar-field potential, current and Cauchy-data form
contents.support: The notes vary a real scalar Lagrangian, obtain theta = -delta(phi) star d(phi), and evaluate the integrated current as the field/momentum pairing. The example performs the computation on a compact flat spatial torus with the Iyer–Wald sign order.

contents.name: Section 3.3: Maxwell gauge transformations and boundary electric charge
contents.support: This is an internal gauge-symmetry example, not a derivation for gravitational diffeomorphisms. The page retains only the general mathematical criterion that a proposed charge one-form must be exact.
contents.reason: This is an internal-gauge model with boundary electric charge, while the assigned page treats spacetime diffeomorphisms and does not transfer that model formula.

contents.name: Infinite-dimensional phase-space regularity caveat in §2.1
contents.support: The notes explicitly describe their infinite-dimensional manifold manipulations as heuristic. The local definition therefore works with finite-dimensional smooth families and asserts no global smooth structure on the full configuration or solution space.
